title: Track changes in a unit of work

task.text: Load accounts, change them freely, and write everything once at commit.
`UnitOfWork(Map<String, Integer> db)` works on a `db` of balances by id. `Account` is given and must stay a plain object.

items: `load(id)` returns one `Account` per id (an identity map), snapshotting its balance. Unknown ids throw `IllegalArgumentException`.
`registerNew(a)` and `registerRemoved(a)` record intent. Nothing touches `db` until `commit()`.

`commit()` returns the log, in this order: `INSERT id` for new accounts, `UPDATE id` for loaded ones whose balance differs from the snapshot, then `DELETE id`. A removed account is only deleted. `db` changes only for the rows in the log.
After `commit()` the unit of work starts clean and can be reused.
`rollback()` restores loaded balances and forgets pending new and removed accounts.

checks.title: One object per id inside a unit of work
Loading an unknown id is rejected
The database is untouched until commit
Commit writes inserts, updates and deletes
Inserts first, then updates, then deletes
A removed object is only deleted
A unit of work can be reused after commit
Commit writes only the rows in its log
Dirty checking compares with the load snapshot

hints.text: The unit of work is a ledger of what happened during one business transaction. It needs to remember three things: what it loaded, what the loaded things looked like, and what was registered.

Keep a `Map<String, Account>` for identity, a `Map<String, Integer>` snapshot of balances, and lists for new and removed accounts. `commit()` compares each loaded account with its snapshot instead of asking the account whether it is dirty.
Commit in three passes over your tracking data:

lines: for (Account a : created) { db.put(a.id, a.balance); log.add("INSERT " + a.id); }
for (Account a : removed) { db.remove(a.id); log.add("DELETE " + a.id); }
